summary: The underlying validator gap still holds, but the exact repro is no longer silent. The loop version exits 0 with a -Wparameter-usage warning and its define void @main() is line-for-line identical (27/27) to the DXIL pasted in 2021: phi float [ %10, %5 ], [ undef, %4 ] feeding fadd, and undef reaching the output when count <= 0. DXIL validation accepts it. The straight-line spelling is still rejected by the validator (E_FAIL 0x80004005, InstrNoReadingUninitialized) on main and on both ends of the release range. The mechanism is one line of source: lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp has bool LegalUndef = isa<PHINode>(&I), so the rule is local and syntactic and PHI nodes are exempt by name -- through the loop, fadd operand is the phi, not literally UndefValue. A local-variable restatement remains completely silent, proving the 2023 out-parameter warning did not close the validator hole. Not optimisation-dependent (-Od reproduces). Related to #3009, #3706, and #3693, but not a duplicate: those exercise direct undef arithmetic, resource indexing, and nested out-of-bounds Sema handling rather than PHI-carried propagation.

The defect itself is untouched, and the warning does not cover it: variant-local-uninit.hlsl (same loop over a local variable instead of an out parameter) is still completely silent -- exit 0, no error, no warning, same undef-seeded phi -- and matches both predicates on main.
